children: Shares of Asset Reconstruction Company (India), or ARCIL, made a muted debut on the stock exchanges on Thursday, September 17, listing at Rs 139 on both the NSE and BSE, exactly in line with the IPO price.

The flat opening came despite strong demand for the Rs 732.97 crore public issue, which was subscribed 20.10 times during the September 9-11 bidding period. Investors placed bids for around 74.20 crore shares against 3.69 crore shares on offer.

Qualified institutional buyers led the demand, with their portion subscribed 52.65 times. The non-institutional investor category was subscribed 15.69 times, while the retail portion was covered 3.39 times.

The stock’s debut also fell short of grey-market expectations. ARCIL shares had commanded a premium of around Rs 12 per share before listing, implying a potential gain of roughly 9 per cent over the issue price. Grey-market premiums are unofficial indicators and do not necessarily translate into actual listing prices.
Entire Issue Was An Offer For Sale
ARCIL’s IPO was entirely an offer for sale, with existing shareholders offloading shares. As a result, the company will not receive any proceeds from the issue.
The selling shareholders included Avenue India Resurgence Pte and State Bank of India, classified as promoters, along with Lathe Investment Pte and Federal Bank.

The company had fixed the IPO price band at Rs 132-139 per share. At the upper end, ARCIL’s implied market capitalisation stood at around Rs 4,516 crore. The lot size was 107 shares, requiring a minimum investment of Rs 14,873 at the upper price band.

ARCIL is an asset reconstruction company registered with the Reserve Bank of India under the SARFAESI Act. Its business involves acquiring stressed and non-performing financial assets from banks, financial institutions and NBFCs and working towards their resolution through restructuring, settlements, enforcement and other recovery mechanisms.

The company operates across corporate loans, SME and other loans, and retail loans. Its revenue streams include trust management fees and returns from investments in security receipts linked to acquired assets.
ARCIL’s revenue rose from Rs 574.1 crore in FY24 to Rs 785 crore in FY26, while operating EBITDA increased from Rs 416.4 crore to Rs 589 crore over the same period.
The flat listing leaves the company’s post-IPO performance dependent on how effectively it can continue resolving stressed assets and generating recoveries from its portfolio.
